summary:
A press release carried by Allwork.Space covers new Camunda research, The AI Process Gap, arguing that broken or pre-AI business processes are the main reason enterprise AI initiatives fail. Headline finding: 72% of organizations say process-related challenges have caused AI initiatives to fail, at an average cost of $1.55 million per business. The same share say AI costs will spiral without better process control, and 82% believe AI investment is wasted without process re-design. The report frames a choice between bolting AI onto legacy processes (seen as lower-friction by 79%) and outcome-centric redesign; 82% say adapting their most important processes will take up to five years, and 61% say redesign cannot keep pace with AI adoption speed.

On governance, 40% of organizations had an AI-related compliance or governance issue in the past 12 months, with process issues contributing to 84% of those. 48% fear AI agents going rogue if processes change, 79% of employees fear their AI use will cause a compliance issue, and 96% expect process challenges to contribute to future incidents. Camunda's Kurt Petersen argues compliance fear is itself slowing the redesign work that would reduce exposure.

A leadership-employee perception gap is highlighted: 89% of organizations say AI boosts team productivity versus 64% of employees; 48% of organizations have rolled back AI use due to negative impact on employees' ability to work; 46% of employees would consider changing jobs over poorly implemented AI. Additional employee data: 69% were not fully consulted, 65% say different implementation would help, 44% have manually overridden AI outputs due to faulty underlying process, and 41% have used AI performatively to satisfy an AI mandate.

Methodology: Sapio Research surveyed 1,000 process decision makers and 5,000 employees across US, UK, Germany and France at organizations of 1,000+ employees, online in July and August 2026. Camunda positions itself as an agentic orchestration platform with governance, auditability and human oversight, used by 700+ organizations.
